tiles.title: Distribution Shape, Outliers, and Frequency Distributions

steps.visual_purpose: Three value spreads side by side, one with the tail trailing right, one trailing left and one trailing evenly both ways, with the long tail visibly marked.
A short list of delivery records with the extreme value highlighted next to the record details that would show whether it is an entry error or a real event.
A frequency table beside the histogram drawn from it, with each bin's count matched to its bar height and the tallest bar marked as the peak.
Scatter plots for a strong positive, a strong negative and a near-zero relationship, each labelled with its correlation value.
A three-by-three correlation matrix with the magnitudes of the pairwise values visible, so signs can be set aside when ranking strength.
A scenario sentence with the entities and their attributes picked out and grouped into candidate tables.
A sample table with each candidate key column marked for repeated or blank values.
Two linked tables with an arrow from the foreign key column to the primary key column and one row whose arrow has no target.
A one-to-many link between customers and orders, with the many side and the foreign key column marked.
One wide orders table repeating customer details, beside the split customers and orders tables linked by a key.
Two tables joined through a junction table, showing two one-to-many links and the combined primary key.
A small ER diagram of customers, orders, products and order items with boxes, ovals, an underlined key and marked relationship lines.
Show a technically-worded sentence alongside its plain-language rewrite, with the substituted words highlighted, so the learner can see exactly where formal terms were replaced or glossed.

Show the same Lagos delivery-time finding written twice side by side: the detail-first, dense version for the operations manager and the recommendation-first, high-level version for the executive, so the structural and density differences are immediately visible.

tiles.title: Structuring Presentations and Writing Executive Summaries

steps.visual_purpose: Show the three-part presentation spine — Opening (context/situation) → Body (finding + evidence) → Call to Action (what is being asked) — so the learner can see how the Lagos example maps onto each slot.

Show a single unbroken paragraph version of an executive summary alongside a correctly structured version with a takeaway title, a 'Finding' section header, and a 'Recommendation' section header, so the learner can see how headers and prose replace bullets and undifferentiated text.
